sections.heading: The Nintendo Game Boy Collection is now 100% hand-written!

bullets.text: I’ve completely updated and rewritten every part of the Game Boy Collection, including the Curator’s Note, all twelve chapters and every game card.

Another step towards a fully European shelf: For the Game Boy I had to leave out some real gems, like the three Final Fantasy Legend games. But it made room for 25 games that had real impact in Europe, such as Asterix, Tintin in Tibet, The Smurfs and Lemmings.

Two new chapters: “Comic Heroes from Europe” and “Home-Computer Hits”. To make room, Sports and Racing now share a chapter, and so do Adventures and RPGs. A few other chapters got a new focus as well, like “Licensed & Movie Tie-ins” and “Cult Classics & Deep Cuts”.

The Collection now uses European titles and release years: Probotector instead of Operation C, Shadow Warriors instead of Ninja Gaiden Shadow, Mystic Quest instead of Final Fantasy Adventure, and so on. The Game Boy only reached Europe in 1990, so nothing here is dated 1989 anymore.

Super Game Boy badges: 25 games now carry a “Super Game Boy” badge: they have their own border, colours or sound when you play them on a SNES through Nintendo’s adapter. The filter finds the badges too.
Pixel corners: I used rounded corners for cards before. These are now replaced by stepped, pixel-style ones that fit the Game Boy theme much better.

sections.heading: Arrange the shelf however you like

bullets.text: The shelf has a new Arrange control. Besides the timeline, you can now group the Collections by maker, by type (home consoles or handhelds) or by status (hand-written or draft in progress).
Your choice is part of the page’s address, so you can share a link to, say, the shelf grouped by maker.

The timeline is now in true launch order, which moves the original Xbox from the end of the shelf to its rightful spot in 2001. I also removed the number on each tile, since it wouldn’t mean much in the new groupings.

Updated typography for game titles: Titles of games, magazines, films and comics used to be bold. They’re now italic, as in editorial style, and tinted slightly towards the colour of the page. This now works the same on every page and in every section. Bold text is now reserved for real emphasis and key terms, which makes it easier to spot what actually matters in the Curator’s Notes.
Controller illustrations: The Game Boy Collection now also has a custom illustration instead of an emoji on the shelf.
Fewer labels: The European perspective is now the default, so I’ve hidden the “EU-first” label on the shelf. The six Collections that aren’t Europe-first yet keep their “NA-first” label for now.

Better contrast: Faint labels, accent-coloured text and chapter colours are now easier to read, in both light and dark mode, across all Collections. Another nice step towards my goal of the entire website passing WCAG accessibility requirements.
Smoother theme switching: Switching between light and dark mode now cross-fades the whole page at once. In Safari, some headings used to lag behind.

Theme choice carries across pages: If you switch between light and dark mode, the site now remembers that while you browse, instead of resetting on every page. It’s only saved for your current visit, so for a new visit it follows your device’s setting again.

Badges: Badges like “PAL-optimised” now sit right next to a game’s number, instead of on the other side of the card. This works better because some Collections have graphic elements in the top right corner of the game card.
I rewrote the description of the site that you see in search results and link previews, to emphasise the project’s European focus.
Fixed a few small Safari glitches, where elements could jump by a pixel while resizing the window.
Diastro Gaming Collections now lives at diastrogaming.com. Nothing else has moved, and old links to diastrocollections.github.io will keep working and bring you right here.

sections.heading: The NES Collection is now 100% hand-written!

bullets.text: Every part of the NES Collection is now written by me: the Curator’s Note, all twelve chapters, every single game.

The first step towards a fully European shelf: Collection by Collection, I’ll update the shelf to only include games that actually came out in Europe. For the NES that meant leaving out some real gems, like Final Fantasy and Dragon Warrior. But it made room for around 30 games that America never got to play, or that Europe simply loved more, such as Asterix, The Smurfs, Fantastic Dizzy and Micro Machines.

Two new chapters: “Home-Computer Hits” and “Zappers, Robots & Party Games”. The removal of Japanese-made RPGs left a huge hole, so that chapter became “Quests & Action-RPGs”. Finally, “Puzzle & Party” became “Puzzle & Co-op”.
The Collection now uses European titles: Probotector instead of Contra, Teenage Mutant Hero Turtles, Street Gangs, Dynablaster, and so on.

More PAL badges: 27 games in the Collection now carry a “PAL-adjusted” or “PAL-optimised” label, up from about a dozen. There are many interesting stories left to tell, and I hope to cover them in the upcoming YouTube videos!
I’ve started replacing the emoji on the shelf with custom controller illustrations. The NES is the first one, and the rest will follow over the next few updates.
I removed the icon next to each Collection’s title on the shelf as well, which makes the tiles a little calmer.
The How it’s made page has a new Copyright and license section.

All text, collection data and original images are licensed under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Feel free to share them, unchanged and with credit, as long as it’s not commercial. The code behind the site is open source under the MIT license.
Every page’s footer now shows which license applies to what.

I’ve adopted a sort-of standard typography ruleset for the project: apostrophes and quotation marks across the whole site are now real curly ones (’ “ ”). Searching still works the way you’d expect, so typing `kirby's` still finds Kirby’s Adventure.
Removed the “Back to the shelf” link from the How it’s made and Version history pages, since the persistent navigation bar already does that job.
The NES Collection’s Curator’s Note and first two chapters are now fully hand-written! While I was at it, a fresh research pass caught a few wrong game titles and release years.
PAL badges: NES cards now show “PAL-adjusted” or “PAL-optimised”, so you can see at a glance which games actually got some love for 50Hz. The filter finds those labels too.
The Game Boy Collection’s Curator’s Note is now hand-written as well.
Navigation bar: a persistent bar at the top of every page, so you can jump to any part of the project from anywhere.
Dark/light toggle: always in the top right corner now, whatever page you’re on.
Back to top: on large screens, a button appears once you’ve scrolled down. Phones don’t get one, because tapping the top of the screen already does the trick.
Chapters drop-down: replaces the chapter chips. It’s cleaner on every screen size and better for accessibility. You can now also link straight to a chapter, e.g. `/nes/#ch-3`.
Previous / next: every Collection now ends with links to its neighbours on the shelf, for when you just want to keep browsing.
Footer: tidied up, with direct links to the AI disclaimer and privacy policy on the How it’s made page.
Screen readers: the whole project is now fully usable with them.
Keyboard: navigation is much improved, and every page now has a skip link. More improvements are on the way!
Colour: this one’s tricky, since the project leans heavily on artistic use of colour. Accessibility matters to me, though, so high-contrast and colourblind modes are on my list.

sections.text: And as always, lots of tiny visual fine-tuning. :D

bullets.text: In the Game Boy Collection, I swapped in Castlevania II: Belmont’s Revenge for Solomon’s Club. I forgot to add an actual Castlevania game to the chapter on Metroidvania! :D
I also found <cite>Solomon’s Club</cite> redundant because block puzzlers are already well represented in the Collection, and it has no unique regional or historical story.
Added “Hand-written” / “Draft in progress” badges on the hub and on every Collection page.
Here you can learn about who I am, how I create, improve and maintain this project.

I also find it very important to be 100% transparent on the use of AI, how I measure site views, my zero-tracking policy, as well as possible ways to financially support the project in the future. Check it out if you get the chance, I appreciate it!

Version history is now dynamic: To support a fun new dynamic release timeline graphic, as well as a possible notification service or Discord bot in the future, I converted the version history from static HTML to JSON data.
Fonts are now self-hosted, so visitor IP addresses no longer go to Google.
The “Report a mistake” email links now fill in the page name in the subject line.
Several styling improvements: Site navigation has improved both on desktop and mobile browsers. Fine-tuned the platform flourishes for the Game Boy, SNES and DS.
The Nintendo DS, Sega Master System and Microsoft Xbox Collections are now live.
They were researched and styled with Claude Cowork (Sonnet 5, High effort), same as before. I’ll be rewriting their stories myself over time, just like the original twelve.
Pushing the styling intensity on the 3 new collections made them noticeably bolder than the original set, so I brought that same energy back to the base collections and the hub page.
CSS cleanup across every theme: 13 theme stylesheets and the hub stylesheet had leftover duplicate code from the styling passes, now consolidated with no visual changes.
Added a graphical timeline to the hub page, with clickable platform markers.
A handful of smaller styling fixes and tweaks throughout.
Added GitHub Pages CMS by Ronan Berder, so I can add and edit content without touching the code.
Data format migration: required converting all 12 original platforms’ game lists from arrays to named objects.
Added OpenGraph tags and images to every page so Link Previews now look right.
Updated hero, footer and hub page texts.
Added meta descriptions to every page.
Added social links (YouTube, Bluesky, Instagram, Threads, X) to the footer of every page
Linked the “Diastro Gaming” hub logo to the YouTube channel
Added this version history page, plus a link to it and a version pill on the hub
Added a “Back to the shelf” link to every collection page
Made the curator’s note collapsible on every collection page, with a short preview and a “read more” toggle
Reorganized the collection page toolbar: search, result count, and the theme toggle now share a row, with the genre chips moved to their own row below
Several minor improvements to styling and layout.
New curator notes added across every collection
Layout optimizations and styling fixes throughout the hub and collection pages
AI disclaimer added to every page
Copyright notice added to every page
Added GoatCounter analytics to every page
Colour and release-year corrections across several collections
Analytics setup groundwork
Documentation updated to reflect the project’s file structure
Styles and HTML refactored across every page
First release: twelve platform collections, 1,200 games, 144 genre chapters
Searchable, filterable collection pages with a shared hub
